# 1.2.84 - one road for an item that changes owner, one gate on it, keys that open only in hand, and a Search that draws from the room's own tables

Two stages on this line, shipped as one train (the owner's Q2): E35 in full - one road for an item that changes owner - and
E14 in two parts - the gate on that road, the keys, the dead's hands, the rifle and item use (part 1), then the item tables,
what a Search draws and the GM's item windows (part 2). A hand-over, a body's loot, a stash rifled, a Palm's steal and a Plant
now each go through one function on a GM, which moves one piece of a stack and refuses a Plant into full pockets without a word
to the victim. That road refuses a move across rooms, in an Eclipse and in a Class Trial, the dead give and take nothing, a
body whose death the asker knows is taken from only by a loot, and the player is told why. Only a key in hand opens another's
bedroom, and a dead owner's bedroom opens in an Investigation. The dead move none of their things, and a stash is rifled once
a time of day. A tier 3 usable restores 3 of its kind. The GM's item tables are found by their flags whatever language each
client is in, and a room's own tables answer a Search first. None of it has been tried at a real table yet (Known gaps);
everything measured below was measured in the test harness or, for the windows' layout, in a Chromium stand-in.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **The item tables are brought up to date when the primary GM's world loads.** A table the module installed under an older
   English name gets today's English name ("DRPG Crime Tools - Tier 3" becomes "DRPG Murder Weapons - Tier 3"); a table built
   in Polish, or one the GM renamed, keeps its name. A description that is still the module's own wording is rewritten in
   today's English, whatever the primary GM's language. A tier 3 usable made before this version gets today's sentence for its
   kind; a text a GM wrote is kept.
3. **A room's own tables now answer a Search before the tier pools.** A room that Room Setup points at a table draws from it
   first, then the GM's tier pools, then the module's built-in lists. A table named "<room> - Truth Bullets" or "<room> - Room
   Keys" no longer answers any Search.
4. **Bedroom keys.** From this version only a key in hand opens another's bedroom: a key put away in a stash opens nothing
   until it is taken out. When a bedroom changes owner, in Room Setup or with `game.drpg.setVaultRoom`, the old owner's keys
   to it, carried or stashed, are taken. The GM reads "{actor} no longer holds the key to {room}: the room is not theirs any more."
   and the old owner "Your key to {room} was taken back: the room is not yours any more." Nothing is taken at the update
   itself: a key an old owner kept from a change made before 1.2.84 still opens that door, so remove it by hand. The keys
   handed out when the world loads count a stashed key as held, so no second key is made beside it.
5. **The "rifles" GM store.** A new GM store, "Which stash each character has gone through, and in which time of day", is
   kept in a setting nobody is shown, synced between the GMs and left out of the backup. It is cleared with the reset group
   "The stashes each student has already found, and every hidden stash open again". It starts empty, so the first free reach
   into each stash after the update counts from then.
6. **Settings, keys and texts.** One new setting nobody is shown (the rifles store); no new setting you see and no new
   keybinding. `lang/en.json` goes from 3739 strings to 3774 (39 added, 4 removed, 17 reworded) and `lang/pl.json` from 4534 to
   4569 (42 added, 7 removed, 24 reworded). The Polish name of the gear group is now "Sprzęt" wherever it is read, where the
   sheet said "Ekwipunek". The new tier pool field's placeholder reads "e.g. DRPG Tools - Tier 2", and the stash notes say
   "once each time of day".

## At the table

### For the GM

- **One gate for every move of an item between two characters.** A hand-over, a body's loot, a stash rifled, a Palm's steal
  and a Plant are refused in an Eclipse, in a Class Trial and across rooms (for a hand-over, two rooms of one name on
  different scenes included). A dead student gives, takes and plants nothing; a body whose death the asker knows is taken
  from only by a loot, and one whose death is kept from them is robbed or planted on as a living student. A steal and a
  Plant are also refused at a Monocub or a Monokuma off the GMs' mark, at a hidden token and at oneself. The refusal reaches
  the player as "That cannot be done now.", "The character is not where it needs to be." or "What it names is not there any
  more."
- **A body is looted only by a living student in its room** who knows of the death, outside an Eclipse and a Class Trial, its
  token not hidden. A Monocub's body is looted as any body. A Take the gate refuses is greyed with its reason in the body's loot
  window, and the window reads it again as the taker or the body moves and as the clock changes.
- **One piece of a stack per action.** Each move takes one piece, and the giver's count is read again after the copy is made.
  A piece used, broken or gone on the way changes no hands, and you read "“{name}” changed on {from}'s sheet while it was on
  its way to {to} - used, broken or gone. Nothing changed hands." A piece that reaches hands holding the same item joins it
  and takes no slot, even in otherwise full hands.
- When a piece could not be taken off the giver, you read one line in that road's words, such as "{to} took “{name}” off
  {from}'s body, but it could not be taken off the body. There is one too many now - remove it from the body's sheet."
- **Copies of an old owner's key** stay with their holders. You read "Copies of the key to {room} are still held by {holders}.
  They open its door for its new owner too; take them away by hand if they should go with the room." Each copy's text the
  module wrote for the old owner is rewritten for the new one.
- **A dead owner's bedroom opens in an Investigation** once the death is published, to everyone; it shuts again after the
  Investigation until you give the room away. A tunnel still passes another's bedroom with no key.
- **A stash is rifled once a time of day** per thief, stash and owner, the Mastermind included. A Search's find is not counted,
  and a reach that moved nothing is taken off the count. A second reach is refused as "That has already been settled." The
  rifle's own refusals are told too: a thief in no room as not where it needs to be, and no stash of that owner here, a hidden
  one not found or the thing gone, alike, as not there any more.
- **The dead keep their hands still.** A dead student's stow, retrieve, use, ready and discard are refused, and their sheet
  offers none of these buttons; a Monocub's sheet offers no Use, Discard or open stash. On the primary GM a dead student's
  stash write is put back, and a lowered count, a break and wear on a body are put back too. A grant into a body's Gear readies
  it with no warning about the dead.
- **Item use.** A tier 3 usable restores 3 of its kind, with no choice and no Hope. A player's discard is filed by the GM's
  browser: Tamper in an Investigation or a Class Trial, for a side of the running incident, or once a body is found;
  Preparation otherwise, whatever type the player's browser sent. A usable's kind is the item tables' where they know its
  name, and Give warns "By the item tables, {item} is {kind}: that decides what it will restore."
- **One creative ruling at a time on an item.** A second card's Works while a ruling is open reads "A ruling on {item} is
  already being made. Answer this card once it is done.", and a card whose item was used up or no longer carried closes with
  "Closed by {name}: the item is used up or no longer carried. Nothing was given."
- An improvised weapon goes into the killer's hand once, and a broken Gear taken out beside one stowed reads "{item} cannot be
  held ready, and only one {group} may be stowed. Take a working one in hand first."
- **What a Search draws.** Your item tables are found by the flags the installer writes, whatever language each client is in;
  the module's built-in lists stay English. A room's tables answer in order: "<room> - Tier N", "<room> - <category>", then
  "<room>", then any other table of the room as a substitute ("Tier N" no higher than the roll, or a category a Search
  draws), then the tier pools, then the built-in lists. The find takes the category, tier and goal of what was drawn, never
  above the tier the roll earned, and its trace and card follow what was found.
- **A Search's plant that could not be handed over goes back to its room**, and you read "{item} is waiting in {room} again:
  the finder could not take it." or "{item} could not go back to {room}, where another planted item waits: it is gone." A
  plant found is told to you as it is taken: "{actor} found {item}, the item planted in {room}."
- **The Item tables window.** The Tier pools tab and a rename there take only a name the module reads as a tier pool, and a
  refusal says "“{name}” is not a tier pool. Name it for a category and a tier, one of: {forms} - where N is a tier from {low}
  to {high}." A table with a tier pool's flags is renamed only to its own category and tier. The Room pools tab takes any other
  name, and "<base> - Tier N" when <base> is a room's table. A refused name stays in its field with the sentence under it. A
  renamed tier pool is one by its flags in this window, in Room Setup and in the draws.
- The window's list rows are one height, an entry is one row with Place and Remove in their own columns, captions stand above
  their boxes, and the item tables, Create an item and the Give windows keep their text at 11 px or more (the stand-in
  measures under Known gaps). The heading drops "DRPG " as the list does.
- **Create an item from a Search** opens on its tab with the room's tables ticked, and says "{room} has no table for this tier
  yet: make “{name}” on the Room pools tab to keep finds of this tier there." when there is none.
- **An item with no category the module knows** is drawn under Other: "Not under any heading: it has no category the game
  knows. Remove it here and give it again from Give / take items as what it is." Its Remove asks "Remove {item} from {actor}?
  It is gone from the sheet for good."
- **Give a room key** says so on its button; with no key left to give it reads "{name} already holds a key to every bedroom
  that has an owner." or "The only bedroom with an owner is {name}'s own. There is no key to give." and the button is off.
  Give a Truth Bullet opens on Write a new one when no trace lies on any scene. A hand-over from a character in no room reads
  "{name} is not standing in any room. Move their token into one first."
- A refused Palm of your own writes no "sent" line on its card.

### For players

- **A Plant into full pockets is refused**, seen or unseen, with a stash or without (the owner's D42). The item stays with you,
  your card reads "{who} has no room for {item}. It stays with you." and then "They felt nothing.", and the other student is
  told nothing. At 1.2.83 the item went into a stash of theirs when they had one, and a seen attempt with no stash told
  them "You catch {who} trying to slip something into your pocket. Nothing of theirs is on you." The action is spent.
- **One action moves one piece of a stack.** Handing over one of several reads "You hand {who} one {name}. You still have
  {left}." What you take with your hands full - off a body, out of a stash or by a Palm - goes into your stash, and without a
  stash it stays where it was; something handed to you over your limit is refused.
- **A key to a room you already hold** is not copied: "You already have a key to {room}. You still hold just the one."
- **When a move is refused** you are told "“{what}” was not carried out." with the reason, such as "The character is not where
  it needs to be." A Palm refused before its dice are read gives the action back ("Your action is back."); one refused after
  them reads "The GM's client refused it." and stays spent.
- **Keys.** Only a key in your hand opens another's bedroom; one in your stash opens nothing. When a room is given away, its old
  owner reads "Your key to {room} was taken back: the room is not yours any more." In an Investigation the bedroom of a
  published death is open.
- **An open stash, once each time of day.** The rifle window reads "Stashes you can reach in {room}: <strong>{who}</strong>.
  Take one thing from each, once each time of day." A second reach is refused, and you read "You have already been through
  {who}'s stash this time of day. Try it again at the next time of day." The sheet's note under a stash reads "You can take one
  thing from each stash listed here, once each time of day."
- **After your character dies** they move nothing: "{name} is dead. What is on the body stays there, to be found." A Monocub's
  things are its body's.
- **A tier 3 usable restores 3 of its kind**, with no choice and no Hope. An item gone from your hands by the time its use's
  window closes reads "{item} is no longer in your hands. Nothing was used."
- **A Search** can hand over another kind of item or a lower tier than you asked for, never a higher one. A hunt for a hidden
  stash from outside any room reads "You go over the room and find nothing anybody has tried to hide."
- **A stash out of reach** says where it is: "Your stash is in {room} - stand there to reach it." or "You have no stash on
  this scene."
- An item with no heading on your sheet reads "Not under any heading yet. Ask the GM to file it."

### For everybody

- **A Search finds the GM's item tables whatever language each client is in**, and a GM in Polish no longer renames a table
  or writes its description in Polish.
- **With no GM connected**, as at 1.2.83 and now checked road by road: a hand-over, a body's loot, a stash rifled, a Palm's
  steal and a Plant each settle at once with one line, and a Palm started then is refused before its window and its price
  with "An action roll waits for a GM: no GM is connected, so the action was not taken and nothing was paid."

## Known gaps

- **LIVE-E35-01** (item 295, not tried yet): a stack of 3 given at a v14 table leaves 2, then 1; measured headless only.
- **LIVE-E35-02** (item 296, not tried yet): an unseen Plant into full pockets shows the victim nothing; measured headless only.
- **LIVE-E14-02** (item 297, not tried yet): Daily Life at a real table with items, a Plant and a loot - the refusals read, a
  stashed key, a rifle twice, and how long a Palm's player waits now that its rows answer "reply".
- **LIVE-E14-01** (item 298, not tried yet): a GM in English, a player in Polish, a Search in a room with a table; with it, the
  Item tables window, Create an item and the Give windows in a real Foundry v14 at 1366x768, both themes, at Foundry's own root
  size, with screenshots of the refused tier pool name.
- **Defaults kept, not yet ruled by the owner**: under an unseen Plant a Gear arrives stowed, so the victim may carry two stowed
  until they ready one; a piece whose twin the taker already carries joins it even in otherwise full hands; a copy of an old
  owner's key stays with its holder (named to the GM) when the room changes owner.
- A hand-over asks the room, both lives and the phase, not the person: a give to a hidden token, a Monocub or a Monokuma goes
  through, as before. A dead receiver of a give is refused as "That cannot be done now.", published or not.
- A loot into full hands with no stash tells the taker only that it was not carried out. A copy that could not be written reads
  as full hands on a steal's, a rifle's and a Plant's card (not driven).
- A loot of a key the taker already holds still marks the body and leaves its Truth Bullet naming that key; a rifle's Search
  card under the same rule names the thief's own key (not driven); and a key whose removal fails tells nobody. A taker whose
  only key to a room is stashed is given the copy.
- A piece moved off a stack keeps the stack's identity, so two items share one. A piece sent to the taker's stash beside a twin
  there makes an item of its own. A name or description changed on the way is copied as first read. A write landing between
  the giver's second read and the count's write is not measured.
- A room whose owner is cleared takes the old owner's keys too; a room given away while the old owner owns one of that name on
  another scene leaves them.
- The rifle window greys no stash already gone through this time of day. Two reaches at once on one GM, and two GMs serving one
  thief at once, are read in the code only. A new time of day is tested by rewriting the store's row, not by moving the clock.
- A Palm refused at the gate's second asking, after its dice, reads only "The GM's client refused it.", read in the code and not
  driven. The body's loot window is not read again when a death is published with the sheet open.
- A crisis replay's use asks no death, by design, and a ready written by a console stands. The dead player's own page on an
  unpublished death, and a reload, are not drawn headless.
- A discard is the GM's type; a player's packet naming another action keeps its Preparation or Tamper type. Two GMs ruling one
  item at once on two browsers are not held against each other, and `game.drpg.grantItemEffect` asks nothing of the item. A
  Tier 0 use as a crisis action still counts as used while it waits.
- A tier 3 usable with no kind (Candy floss, in both tier 3 pools, or a console grant with none) still asks Health or Sanity at
  its use, as a kindless usable does at every tier.
- Give's kind warning is drawn headless only. Other's "weapon" and "armor" are Daggerheart's type names as recalled, not read;
  its Remove leaves no trace and no ledger row.
- The GM's plant window takes a name only, so a plant's category is read off its name, else the Search's ask. A Reroll's
  refused plant goes back without a word to the GMs.
- The Item tables window lists a table named "<room> - " and any words with that room, while a Search there takes it only with
  a suffix the module reads.
- In the stand-in the Stained Glass Item tables window's Room pools tab runs past 768 px; the checkbox colour, "Tell the player"
  under Daggerheart's orange and the hub's width on v14 are not measured. The Polish player handbook names the sheet's tab
  *Ekwipunek*, Daggerheart's word, beside "Sprzęt" for the group.
- The Monocub's panel sentence in the GM handbook stays as it is until a later stage replaces it, and no test reads the new
  handbook sentences. The Polish of the new lines was written and read by the implementers only.
- Not driven by a test: a player with two characters, a Mastermind thief at a concealed stash, a victim leaving between the roll
  and the run, a seen, a missed and a critical Palm from a player's page, a stow's and a retrieve's road to the out-of-reach
  line, a Reroll's trace, the late road of a plant check, and a room's skip of a tier pool among its other tables.
- Known leaks whose stages have not shipped are unchanged.
